stories.summary: The Llanos are the great plains of the Orinoco basin, where cattle ranching, the llanero and the joropo, played with harp, cuatro and maracas, are the best-known traditions.

unit.title: Venezuela II: The Llanos, Tepuis & Modern Diaspora

stories.summary: The Gran Sabana and Canaima National Park, a UNESCO site since 1994, are known for their tepuis and for Angel Falls, called Kerepakupai Merú by the Pemón.

stories.title: La crisis económica y la hiperinflación

unit.title: Venezuela II: The Llanos, Tepuis & Modern Diaspora

stories.summary: After the fall of the oil price in 2014 Venezuela went through a deep crisis with hyperinflation; the government blames sanctions, its critics blame economic policy and corruption, and in 2026 the political situation changed.

stories.title: El éxodo venezolano

unit.title: Venezuela II: The Llanos, Tepuis & Modern Diaspora

stories.summary: According to UNHCR about 7.9 million Venezuelans were living abroad at the end of 2025, most of them in Latin American countries such as Colombia, which created a temporary protection status in 2021.

stories.summary: Venezuelans abroad have taken their arepas and their music with them, from precooked maize flour to the orchestras of El Sistema, while many feel the distance from their families.
